nodes.label: Simatrix Platform
nodes.rationale: A platform of interactive simulations helping B.Tech students build intuition for engineering concepts across disciplines; each sim ships as a sandboxed iframe payload teaching as a Guided Stepper. Success = a struggling first-year understands the first step in 30 seconds and can verify a textbook problem.

nodes.label: Guided Stepper
nodes.rationale: A progressive-disclosure wizard that sequences one concept at a time, moving the learner through Orient then Intuition then Problem-solving; replaces the overwhelming all-controls-at-once dashboard.

nodes.label: Brand Personality (Patient, Encouraging, Clear)
nodes.rationale: A warm one-on-one tutor sitting beside the student; encouragement delivered only through tone and a quiet sense of progress, never through game mechanics (no points/streaks/badges/confetti/mascots). Reference lane: GeoGebra, Desmos, Wokwi, Falstad, Tinkercad.

nodes.label: Anti-References (Product Boundaries)
nodes.rationale: Five locked-out boundaries: Gamified EdTech, Glossy/architectural-viz aesthetic, Marketing-site polish, Hard industry-tool mimicry, and the Overwhelming dashboard; they set the boundary for visual, interaction, and copy decisions on every screen.

nodes.label: Seven Core Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Seven strategic principles that override taste in conflicts and apply uniformly across all disciplines: struggling-learner-first, one-idea-per-step, one-language-many-disciplines, show-real-values, educational-scaffolding-industry-vocabulary, inclusive-by-default, and quiet-chrome-loud-subject.

nodes.label: Design for the Struggling Learner First
nodes.rationale: The tie-breaker meta-principle: when a decision helps the confident student but risks losing the anxious first-year, the weaker learner wins. Deliberately NOT a RULES.md checklist item because it cannot be mechanically verified.
nodes.norm_label: design for the struggling learner first

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome, Loud Subject
nodes.rationale: Every UI pixel that is not the simulation viewport stays quiet enough that the math/geometry is what the eye lands on; restrained color (~10% blue accent), minimal decoration, no surface that competes with sim content.

nodes.label: Module 1 — Foundations of Projection
nodes.rationale: Seven live 3D guided-stepper lessons on one shared engine: five intro lessons (reference planes, types of lines, dimensioning, four quadrants, first-angle projection) plus two simulations (Projection of Points, Projection of Straight Lines).

nodes.label: Module 2 — Orthographic Projection of Solids
nodes.rationale: The master codebase: six gated steps flattening a hard-edged solid (cube, prism, pyramid, cylinder, cone) to a 2D orthographic drawing, with a parameter dock, rotation priority hierarchy, and vertex labeling; every change funnels through one rebuild() pipeline.

nodes.label: Compare View
nodes.rationale: The main pane is always the live 3D scene; the 2D textbook drawing (or a live-rebuilt 3D view while folded) appears on demand in a floating Compare card, with a docked side-by-side split for Points/Lines.

nodes.label: Cinematic Reversible Fold/Unfold
nodes.rationale: The HP plane hinges flat onto the VP about the xy fold line and back again, either holding the learner's own 3D viewing angle (Points/Lines) or sweeping square-on (First-angle).

nodes.label: Lines Workbench
nodes.rationale: The expanded Compare split collapses the wizard for a true 50/50 and docks the live driver controls (True Length, distance HP/VP, theta, phi) under both panes (ADR-021) — the one deliberate exception to progressive disclosure, for the solve-and-verify phase.

nodes.label: Problem Library
nodes.rationale: Tiered textbook problems with hints revealed one at a time and a ±0.5-tolerant self-check that never auto-fills; the student dials the setup and the check lights green, making the sim a verification tool not a toy.

nodes.label: Inline Term Glossary
nodes.rationale: Dotted-underline terms open a tooltip on hover/focus/click fed by per-lesson TERMS data, providing an inline definition the first time a textbook term appears without replacing the term itself.

nodes.label: Dual Perspective/Orthographic Camera
nodes.rationale: Top/Front/Side orthographic quick-view chips with a perspective-to-ortho morph, plus clip-aware auto-zoom and a connector/projector declutter toggle.

nodes.label: Parameter Dock
nodes.rationale: Module 2's uiManager controls: base length, height, distance HP/VP, angle HP/VP, manual Y rotation; every slider paired two-way with a clamped numeric input tolerating a decimal comma.

nodes.label: Accessibility Commitments (WCAG 2.2 AA)
nodes.rationale: WCAG 2.2 AA target: color never the only signal (two-cue rule), contrast, full keyboard access with visible focus, reduced-motion honored, screen-reader announcements, and legibility-first Atkinson Hyperlegible typography. Accessibility is a defining goal, not a compliance afterthought.

nodes.label: Primary Persona — Struggling First-Year
nodes.rationale: The person every decision is optimized for: a first-year who finds orthographic projection abstract and intimidating, with no CAD/MATLAB exposure, who quietly assumes they are 'bad at this'. Used across self-study, classroom, and assessment contexts.

nodes.label: Points/Lines Fold Swoop (Module 1)
nodes.rationale: The shared engine's held-angle dolly replaced by animateFoldSwoop/snapFoldSwoop on the dual-camera stack: forward engages the ortho camera and glides it front-on to the flattened sheet morphing perspective to ortho on the easeFold curve; drives both Module 1 sims (Points via main.js, Lines via lines.js).

nodes.label: Lines Side-by-Side Compare Split
nodes.rationale: Opening Lines Compare collapses the step panel and docks the True Length/distance/angle sliders in a slim strip beneath the two drawings (live 3D left, 2D orthographic right) for a true 50/50 split, replacing the floating PiP card that hovered over the 3D view.

nodes.label: HT/VT Trace Markers
nodes.rationale: HT/VT trace markers now appear in the live 3D scene during the 'Show Traces' walkthrough — a teal dot where the line pierces HP, an amber dot where it pierces VP, each with a dashed extension — so traces read in 3D, not only in the 2D construction (off-sheet traces suppressed).

nodes.label: Lines 5-Step Problem-Solving Stepper
nodes.rationale: The Lines sim reworked into a 5-step stepper (True Length, Distance from HP/VP, Inclinations, Generate Orthographic Projections, Draw Traces) built on one general line the learner sets up, each step exposing only its own control, replacing six fixed-orientation exploration steps.

nodes.label: N.D. Bhatt / K.C. John Textbook Problem Sets
nodes.rationale: Authentic N.D. Bhatt / K.C. John textbook problem sets for the Points and Lines Problem Libraries (points across the four quadrants plus on-plane cases; lines from parallel-to-both through inclined-to-both), with flexible 'OR' answer acceptance for geometrically degenerate quadrants.
nodes.norm_label: n.d. bhatt / k.c. john textbook problem sets

nodes.label: Dual-Camera Orchestrator Port
nodes.rationale: Ported Module 2's full camera/animation orchestrator into the shared engine — dual perspective/orthographic cameras with active-camera switching, a projection-matrix morph (projectionMorphK) for seamless 3D<->2D transitions, clip-aware auto-zoom, orthographic quick-views, and a flattened 2D pan — gated to the Points/Lines sims.

nodes.label: Points/Lines Auto-Zoom Framing
nodes.rationale: Engine hardening: the auto-zoom frames the subject on the geometry's centre so the camera pulls back linearly as a parameter grows (killing the off-centre 'exponential lurch'), and the view opens snug on the default geometry, easing back only as values grow, via Module 2's one-shot fixed-duration eased dolly.

nodes.label: Step-Card Scrollbar Pill (Module 1)
nodes.rationale: shell.css .step-card's fully-hidden scrollbar replaced with the platform floating padded pill (ADR-032): 10px WebKit channel, transparent track, --color-border thumb floating clear via a 3px transparent padding-box border, with a Firefox @supports guard. Hiding a scrollbar fails Visibility of System Status.

nodes.label: Floating Minimal Scrollbars (Module 2)
nodes.rationale: Backported the floating minimal scrollbars (ADR-032) to #step-card and .problem-library__body — the hidden scrollbar replaced by a 10px WebKit channel with a ~4px --color-border pill floating clear via a 3px transparent padding-box border, so learners get a 'more content below' cue in the Quiet-Chrome style.

nodes.label: White Card/Chip Surfaces
nodes.rationale: White card/chip surfaces (--color-host-white) so the sim blends with the white host page when embedded.

nodes.label: Bearing Block Model
nodes.rationale: The orbitable 3D split plummer/pillow block is the lesson subject because it yields all four BIS line types in one view and makes visible edges become hidden edges as it spins; the body no longer redraws the full base slab to avoid non-manifold 'spiderweb' edges and false occlusion.

nodes.label: Hidden-Line Occlusion Raycaster
nodes.rationale: The CPU line-of-sight occlusion raycaster (accelerated by three-mesh-bvh) is REQUIRED, not an optimisation: it makes the visible-Type-A vs hidden-Type-E/F decision that produces dashed lines, the topic's whole reason to exist. Phase 3 tried to drop it for a GPU depth-buffer X-ray and broke the lesson; it was reverted (ADR-029 addendum / ADR-030). Runs live per rAF on orbit.

nodes.label: Front View Projection Morph
nodes.rationale: A dual-camera projectionMorphK matrix blend eases perspective to orthographic so the Front View lands on a true parallel elevation with no 'pop'; dragging or scrolling out eases smoothly back to free-orbit 3D via a single guarded morph so a continued gesture can't fight it.

nodes.label: Line Classification Fixes
nodes.rationale: Math/classification-layer fixes in lineDrawer.js: a coplanar-coverage flush-seam filter drops the false body/foot seam, edge subdivision into ~0.5-unit sub-segments lets a long arris draw solid then dashed exactly where it leaves view, and negating buried contact-face normals stops genuine creases self-occluding while orbiting.

nodes.label: BIS Line-Type Stepper
nodes.rationale: Four-step guided reveal (Type A / Type E-F / Type G / Type B) driven by foundationSteps.js; adds strict BIS 3:1 solid-filled arrowheads, an Aligned vs Unidirectional dimension-text toggle, and an 'Inspect arrowhead' micro-zoom, so completion latches the moment Type B dimensions are revealed.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar (Foundations)
nodes.rationale: The step-card scroll region shows a floating padded pill tinted to --color-border (ADR-032 Quiet Chrome) instead of a hidden scrollbar, giving a 'more content below' cue; scrollbar-width stays unset on the base rule so Chrome 121+ keeps the WebKit pseudo-elements.

nodes.label: Rabattement Fold (Flatten-to-2D)
nodes.rationale: The step-4 fold is a dual-camera event: swoopToAnswerSheet flies an OrthographicCamera square-on while projectionMorphK blends perspective to orthographic over the 1600 ms easeFold hinge, so the folded corner reads as a true flat first-angle drawing; restorePerspective glides back to the 3D orbit.

nodes.label: Orbital Quadrant Flights
nodes.rationale: flyCamera sweeps a TRUE spherical orbit (quaternion slerp of the offset direction + radius/pivot lerp) and each Q1-Q4 pose sits physically inside its own room, so an east-west walk genuinely crosses behind the VP wall instead of cutting a straight chord through the corner.

nodes.label: HP/VP Plane Pair
nodes.rationale: hvPlanes.js draws the teal HP / amber VP pair with faint fills and a dense 'cage' grid; the beyond-fold extension is always built and faded independently via setExtendedOpacity so the shared Quadrant-I corner never re-fades or double-draws, and the HP sits in a pivot hinged on the X fold line. VP sheet border is solid amber by explicit override of the Two-Cue dash pairing.

nodes.label: Point Projector Rig
nodes.rationale: point.js draws P (ink sphere + paper halo) and its thick-dot top/front views p and p', with dashed fat-line projectors starting SPHERE_GAP off P so the dash begins cleanly at the sphere surface (Linux GL dash-shader fix); the on-VP p'-to-fold-line connector stays solid while the 3D VP projector stays dashed.

nodes.label: Frustum Illustration
nodes.rationale: frustums.js draws the step-5 classic textbook figure: cone frustums in Quadrants I and III (Q3 the point-reflection) with concentric-circle top views on HP and trapezoid front views on VP; the Q3 body carries renderOrder -3 so it draws beneath the translucent sheet grids for the 'cage' read and the transparent-to-opaque flip stays seamless.

nodes.label: Spatial Quadrant Label Layer
nodes.rationale: labelLayer.js owns the CSS2D HP/VP/XY callouts, boxed P/p/p' chips and I-IV quadrant numerals; a per-frame updateOcclusion raycasts camera to numeral against the sheet FILL meshes (Line2 grids excluded) and hides occluded numerals, running after renderer.render and before the CSS2D re-projection.

nodes.label: Transition Cross-Fades
nodes.rationale: A per-leaf fadeState opacity multiplier (re-stamped after every rebuild so a mid-fade rebuild never snaps) plus an always-disposed fade-out graveyard let applyView fade planes up on grow and cross-fade the point rig against the frustums across the 4-5 boundary; steps 1-3 carry foldPose:'unfolded' so back-nav auto-reverses the fold.

nodes.label: Room & Shadow Stepper
nodes.rationale: A Module-2-pattern guided-step controller (stepper.js) rendering the 5-step 'Room & Shadow' sequence (Reference Planes to Standard) from pure-data spatialSteps.js, gating Next behind the step-4 fold and pushing each step's view flags to the orchestrator via applyView.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar (Spatial)
nodes.rationale: The #step-card scrollbar pill was retinted from --color-accent to --color-border per ADR-032 Quiet Chrome (WebKit thumb + Firefox scrollbar-color).

nodes.label: Compare Workbench
nodes.rationale: Expanding Compare opens a true 50/50 split (ADR-037): the wizard collapses, the live 3D viewport takes the left pane, the 2D orthographic drawing the right, and the four point drivers re-parent into a docked workbench rail. Built standalone in the topic's own architecture, NOT via engine config keys (Points is off engine.js, ADR-033); the single-WebGL-canvas invariant is kept because the right pane reuses the live 2D canvas. A remeasureAfterReflow waits a second frame so the renderer sizes to the true pane.

nodes.label: Fold Swoop
nodes.rationale: The step-5 fold swoops square-on to the orthographic answer sheet (ADR-036, overturning ADR-013's held-angle hold): driveFold forward calls swoopToAnswerSheet (engage ortho, glide front-on, morph perspective to ortho on easeFold) and reverse glides back via restorePerspective; the held-angle movers and the now-unused preFoldPose/FRAME_PADDING are deleted, so the perspective camera never moves during the fold.

nodes.label: Compare 2D Drawing
nodes.rationale: main.js drawCompare() live-repaints a plain 2D canvas from the point data every rebuild (never a snapshot): a FIXED scale keyed to the 40 mm slider max so 10 mm always reads as 10 mm, the lateral PP coordinate drawn as marks sliding off a centre datum, and paper-halo view marks per ADR-016; the projector is a solid Type-B thin line (only 3D pictorial projectors stay dashed).

nodes.label: Dual-Camera Ortho Quick-Views
nodes.rationale: A second OrthographicCamera + its own OrbitControls make the Top/Front/Side quick-views TRUE orthographic reads (RULES.md 5.18); a projectionMorphK matrix morph lerps the ortho projection from the perspective one and back so the hand-off gains/loses depth smoothly. Every camera-move seam hands the live camera back to perspective first so the two cameras never fight. The rogue single-camera ADR-035 was removed.

nodes.label: Ortho Orbit Lock
nodes.rationale: A quick-view / flat read is a square-on 2D view, so orthoControls.enableRotate is false (pan + zoom stay live); a left-drag on the locked ortho camera fires a qv-lock-cue shake + focus-ring nudge on the latched chip.

nodes.label: Points Quadrant Numeral Occlusion
nodes.rationale: labelLayer.updateOcclusion raycasts camera to each I-IV numeral against the sheet FILL meshes (Line2 grids excluded since their raycast needs Raycaster.camera) and hides any occluded numeral, so numerals no longer read through the HP/VP sheets; numerals were also pushed to the far grid corners to stop clashing with P/p/p'.

nodes.label: Points Problem Library
nodes.rationale: pointProblems.js ports the K.C. John / N.D. Bhatt textbook point problems in three tiers; problemLibrary.js is a data-driven +/-0.5 mm-tolerant OR-array self-check that never auto-fills (on-plane cases keep OR-array targets so a zero-distance point grades correct in either coincident quadrant, ADR-015), loading a problem resets to defaults and routes to Step 1 so the learner dials the answer by hand.

nodes.label: Points Pipeline Migration
nodes.rationale: The topic was cut from the Module 2 skeleton onto the orchestrator pattern (ADR-033): solid generators, shapeData.js, meshAnalyzer/projectionDrawer/vertexLabeler were stripped (a dimensionless point has no edges to weld) and pointData.js + the polished hvPlanes.js/point.js were ported verbatim from the Spatial Framework sibling.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar (Introduction)
nodes.rationale: Backported the platform floating minimal scrollbars (ADR-032) to #shape-rail and #anatomy-panel: a 10px WebKit channel with a ~4px --color-border pill floating clear via a padding-box border, plus a Firefox @supports fallback, giving a 'more content below' cue.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar (Simple Positions)
nodes.rationale: Backported the platform floating minimal scrollbars (ADR-032) to #step-card and .problem-library__body: a 10px WebKit channel with a ~4px --color-border pill floating clear via a padding-box border, plus a Firefox @supports fallback.

nodes.norm_label: north star: the patient tutor's paper

nodes.label: ADR-001: No build step; pinned CDN ES modules
nodes.rationale: Sims ship as self-contained payloads served from an arbitrary URL prefix; must run with zero toolchain, work offline after first CDN fetch, and stay reproducible via a pinned three@0.160.0. Bundlers rejected as they break the open-the-folder-and-run contract.
nodes.norm_label: adr-001: no build step; pinned cdn es modules

nodes.label: ADR-002: Host integration via window.simAPI, not postMessage
nodes.rationale: The sim is only the iframe payload; the surrounding host site is out of scope. A tiny synchronous global API (pause/resume/reset) plus a static meta.json is the smallest possible contract, needing no message protocol or origin negotiation.
nodes.norm_label: adr-002: host integration via window.simapi, not postmessage

nodes.label: ADR-003: CSS design tokens are the single runtime source of truth
nodes.rationale: One identifiable visual language across all subjects: viewport linework and UI chrome can never disagree on a value, and a re-theme is a token swap not a code hunt. Hard-coding hex per use-site is banned.
nodes.norm_label: adr-003: css design tokens are the single runtime source of truth

nodes.label: ADR-004: Every geometry change funnels through one rebuild() pipeline
nodes.rationale: WebGL context exhaustion is the most likely late-stage bug; without one disciplined disposal point geometries/materials/label DOM leak and the context dies. One pipeline keeps scene, projections, labels, and self-check bus in the same state in a fixed order.
nodes.norm_label: adr-004: every geometry change funnels through one rebuild() pipeline

nodes.label: ADR-005: Re-derive ported signs visually; explicit ZXY Euler
nodes.rationale: Unity is left-handed Y-up, Three.js right-handed Y-up; copying Unity's negative signs verbatim produces plausible-but-wrong mirrored projections. Three.js defaults to XYZ Euler so the ZXY order is pinned in one helper.
nodes.norm_label: adr-005: re-derive ported signs visually; explicit zxy euler

nodes.label: ADR-006: Fat lines + hard-edge geometry + quantized edge welding
nodes.rationale: LineBasicMaterial caps at 1px on most GPUs but engineering line weights must be real constant pixels; hard edges keep the CAD outline crisp; welding to 1e-3 collapses duplicate rim lines on curved solids.
nodes.norm_label: adr-006: fat lines + hard-edge geometry + quantized edge welding

nodes.label: ADR-007: Orchestrator + leaf modules; only genericSolid shared
nodes.rationale: A strict no-cross-import rule keeps the dependency graph a star around the orchestrator, so any leaf can be read/replaced without tracing sibling webs; shared trig funnels into one importable pure-function module without stateful coupling.
nodes.norm_label: adr-007: orchestrator + leaf modules; only genericsolid shared

nodes.label: ADR-008: Rotation priority hierarchy via mutually-exclusive UI
nodes.rationale: Rotation modes can conflict; a strict UI-enforced precedence (face inclination > orient preset > manual Y) prevents contradictory states. Pentagonal preset is 54 degrees not 18 - a corrected geometry value recorded so it is not reverted.
nodes.norm_label: adr-008: rotation priority hierarchy via mutually-exclusive ui

nodes.label: ADR-009: No shared library; topic clones are manual full copies
nodes.rationale: With no build step there is no place for a shared library; full duplication keeps each topic an independently-deployable payload and lets a clone drop features freely without risking the master. Cost: copies drift and fixes must be hand-re-copied.
nodes.norm_label: adr-009: no shared library; topic clones are manual full copies

nodes.label: ADR-010: DESIGN.shared.md duplicated per module (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Interim per-module duplication accepted only because no shared root existed yet; superseded by ADR-022 once the root arrived.

nodes.label: ADR-011: Module 1 uses shared engine.js + thin pages (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Seven copy-pasted pages that drifted apart were lifted onto one shared frame so a change lands once; Module 1 draws points/lines not solids so needs no shape generators. Superseded by ADR-033 (full orchestrator migration) - kept for historical record; do not resurrect engine.js for new work.
nodes.norm_label: adr-011: module 1 uses shared engine.js + thin pages (superseded)

nodes.label: ADR-012: On-demand Compare View replaced persistent dual-pane
nodes.rationale: The single-canvas cinematic fold is the hero interaction; the alternate view appears on demand rather than a permanently half-sized split, giving more screen to the 3D teaching. Introduces the no-transform invariant for the fixed-position Compare canvas.
nodes.norm_label: adr-012: on-demand compare view replaced persistent dual-pane

nodes.label: ADR-013: The fold camera moves (revised, then re-overturned)
nodes.rationale: The old 'camera never moves during the fold' rule was deliberately overturned for a Module-2 cinematic; the held-angle revision was later re-overturned by ADR-036. Never re-cite 'camera never moves' as binding.
nodes.norm_label: adr-013: the fold camera moves (revised, then re-overturned)

nodes.label: ADR-014: Auto-zoom is a one-shot eased dolly; tight-fit XOR push-back
nodes.rationale: A per-frame exponential follow read as an accelerating lurch; one eased dolly per rebuild is proportional. Running tight-fit and push-back in one rebuild strands the camera as the tweens fight.
nodes.norm_label: adr-014: auto-zoom is a one-shot eased dolly; tight-fit xor push-back

nodes.label: ADR-015: Self-check is +/-0.5-tolerant, never auto-fills
nodes.rationale: Auto-filling defeats the teaching; a limitation the student can see and manipulate teaches the distinction. OR-arrays only for genuinely degenerate geometry (on-plane/origin points where quadrants coincide).

nodes.label: ADR-016: Drawing line conventions follow N.D. Bhatt / ISO
nodes.rationale: Textbook represents a point as a thick dot; in the 2D drawing HP/VP is carried by position so solid Type-B projectors are standards-correct, while 3D pictorials keep dashed projectors. Do not 'fix' these back - they look like regressions but are deliberate.
nodes.norm_label: adr-016: drawing line conventions follow n.d. bhatt / iso

nodes.label: ADR-017: Lines sim is a 5-step build-up, not six fixed cases
nodes.rationale: Building up one general line teaches the process of constructing a line's views; dedicated per-step controls keep each step to one idea and let dialled values persist across navigation.
nodes.norm_label: adr-017: lines sim is a 5-step build-up, not six fixed cases

nodes.label: ADR-018: Textbook fidelity over fudging; scale 1 unit = 10 mm
nodes.rationale: A limitation the student can see and manipulate teaches the drafting distinction, whereas a silently-adjusted number teaches nothing. Units reconciled by a declared scale (a relabel, not a world rescale - toW(v)=v/10 unchanged).
nodes.norm_label: adr-018: textbook fidelity over fudging; scale 1 unit = 10 mm

nodes.label: ADR-019: Verify sims headlessly via Node built-in WebSocket CDP
nodes.rationale: Installing puppeteer would violate the no-build/no-dependency contract; Node's built-in WebSocket makes a dependency unnecessary. The final green check must run the shipped module, not a hand-typed replica (a replica once passed while the real file had a call-site bug).
nodes.norm_label: adr-019: verify sims headlessly via node built-in websocket cdp

nodes.label: ADR-020: 'Simple Positions' carries no topic number; folder names hide the master
nodes.rationale: The human title was a user preference; the folder naming encodes host-catalog grouping, not the master-to-deploy lineage - a newcomer cannot infer from the names that each folder is a copy of Module2 (a known issue).
nodes.norm_label: adr-020: 'simple positions' carries no topic number; folder names hide the master

nodes.label: ADR-021: Lines expanded Compare enters a 50/50 'workbench'
nodes.rationale: The reserved wizard width halved only the leftover space, so neither canvas reached a true 50/50 (Quiet-chrome violation). Collapsing the wizard reclaims full width; re-parenting the existing driver nodes (not mirroring) keeps one source of truth so listeners/self-check keep working.
nodes.norm_label: adr-021: lines expanded compare enters a 50/50 'workbench'

nodes.label: ADR-022: Platform design system centralized into one root DESIGN.md
nodes.rationale: Enacts the end state ADR-010 was waiting for; the two DESIGN.shared.md copies had drifted ~2 lines, and one root file removes the drift surface. The merge was also a correctness audit resolving stale doc claims in the code's favour.
nodes.norm_label: adr-022: platform design system centralized into one root design.md

nodes.label: ADR-023: PRODUCT.md centralized into one root file
nodes.rationale: Parallels ADR-022: two byte-identical per-module copies were a latent drift point; one root file removes it. The merge audit flagged two real gaps (unimplemented Shift+arrow finer steps; Module 1 mobile-notice wording divergence).
nodes.norm_label: adr-023: product.md centralized into one root file

nodes.label: ADR-024: Topic folders named graphics_module_M_topic_K_slug
nodes.rationale: The host catalogs sims by subject module then by ordered topic; encoding both indices lets the host and a human read grouping/order from the name. The numbers serve the catalog, not the master-to-deploy lineage (documents the rationale ADR-020 left descriptive).

nodes.label: ADR-025: New subject picks its template by geometry (M2=3D, M1=2D)
nodes.rationale: Module2 is the master and most-documented codebase; a 3D subject directly reuses its orchestrator, rebuild pipeline, and fat-line linework, so geometry is the natural template selector.
nodes.norm_label: adr-025: new subject picks its template by geometry (m2=3d, m1=2d)

nodes.label: ADR-029: Foundations adopts orchestrator pattern, retains meshAnalyzer
nodes.rationale: First, partial supersession of ADR-011 (Foundations only): a Module-1 subject built on Module 2's orchestrator with a copied meshAnalyzer and a per-edge line-of-sight occlusion classifier because it teaches on a 3D bearing block.
nodes.norm_label: adr-029: foundations adopts orchestrator pattern, retains meshanalyzer

nodes.label: ADR-030: three-mesh-bvh via CDN import map accelerates occlusion
nodes.rationale: A BVH turns each occlusion ray from a linear triangle scan into ~O(log n), letting the hidden-line pass re-run every frame on the non-convex Bearing Block; added through the import map to stay inside the no-build pinned-CDN contract (ADR-001).
nodes.norm_label: adr-030: three-mesh-bvh via cdn import map accelerates occlusion

nodes.label: ADR-031: rAF-throttle on-orbit hidden-line update, never debounce
nodes.rationale: A debounce only masks a slow recompute and desyncs lines from the part; enabled by the BVH the pass is cheap enough to run every frame (dirty-gated on camera movement) so edges flip visible/hidden live under orbit.
nodes.norm_label: adr-031: raf-throttle on-orbit hidden-line update, never debounce

nodes.label: ADR-033: Module 1 fully adopts orchestrator pattern platform-wide
nodes.rationale: Fully supersedes ADR-011: Quadrants, First-angle, Points, and Lines migrate off shared engine.js onto Module 2's orchestrator + leaf pattern; Quadrants + First-angle ship combined as the Spatial Framework topic.
nodes.norm_label: adr-033: module 1 fully adopts orchestrator pattern platform-wide

nodes.label: ADR-036: Restore front-on ortho camera swoop during the fold
nodes.rationale: Overturns ADR-013's held-angle revision so the fold lands square-on the orthographic answer sheet exactly as the textbook prints it; held-angle dolly (animateFoldHold) retired. Frame the hinge in the sweep's path rather than abandon the square-on landing.
nodes.norm_label: adr-036: restore front-on ortho camera swoop during the fold

nodes.label: ADR-037: Points Compare gains a standalone 50/50 workbench
nodes.rationale: Parity with the Lines workbench (ADR-021) but built in the topic's own standalone architecture (DOM re-parent + body.compare-split grid), not via engine cfg keys which no longer exist since Points migrated off engine.js (ADR-033). Strikes ADR-021's 'Points omits workbenchControls' clause.
nodes.norm_label: adr-037: points compare gains a standalone 50/50 workbench

nodes.label: ADR-038: 2D Compare drawing is a fixed sheet-locked scale
nodes.rationale: The orthographic sheet is a measured drawing; an auto-fit would shrink 10 mm as the line grows, breaking '10 mm reads as 10 mm' and making the 3D-to-2D comparison meaningless. The ADR-014 auto-zoom is for the 3D perspective pane only.
nodes.norm_label: adr-038: 2d compare drawing is a fixed sheet-locked scale

nodes.label: ADR-039: Repository flattening into one unified monorepo
nodes.rationale: Every topic/module sub-repo's inner .git was deleted and collapsed into one Simatrix monorepo to match the centralized root docs and enable atomic platform-wide commits + centralized git hooks; detached sub-repo histories dropped deliberately.
nodes.norm_label: adr-039: repository flattening into one unified monorepo

nodes.label: ADR-040: Cool-neutral clinical palette remap
nodes.rationale: The four clinical neutrals (panel, ink, ink-secondary, border) were re-derived from a clinical LAB source and cooled off their former warm values across all 7 :root sites; the ink-blue accent and every HP/VP/PP domain encoding were left untouched so Quiet-Chrome and Two-Cue still hold.

nodes.label: ADR-041: Split HP/VP dimension groups + filled BIS arrowheads
nodes.rationale: projectionDrawer emits hpDimensionGroup + vpDimensionGroup so the front-view dims fold flat WITH the VP during the Step-6 fold while top-view dims stay put; a single dimension group could not survive the fold. Arrowheads switched to filled 3:1 triangles to match the exam-grade BIS wedge.
nodes.norm_label: adr-041: split hp/vp dimension groups + filled bis arrowheads

nodes.label: Orthographic Projection of Solids (Module 2 master lesson)
nodes.norm_label: orthographic projection of solids (module 2 master lesson)

nodes.label: Camera-Dependent Edge Classification (visible vs hidden, meshAnalyzer + BVH raycaster)
nodes.norm_label: camera-dependent edge classification (visible vs hidden, meshanalyzer + bvh raycaster)

nodes.label: Simatrix Starter Template
nodes.rationale: The stripped, platform-only boilerplate a new subject module (Case C) duplicates. Minted from the Module 2 master with all Engineering-Graphics domain content stripped. Deliberately silent on EG-specific architecture so a new discipline decides and documents its own; ships an empty rebuild() pipeline, working stepper, Compare scaffolding, simAPI, meta.json, fonts, boot watchdog and mobile notice, and nothing subject-specific.

nodes.label: Platform-Wide Contract
nodes.rationale: The only documentation a new subject inherits automatically (the template plus PLATFORM-RULES.md); everything else about how the module is built is the author's to decide and record before writing simulation code.

nodes.label: window.simAPI Host Contract
nodes.rationale: Exposes pause()/resume()/reset(); the in-sim Reset is the only reset path (simAPI.reset()). Host-embed contract chosen over postMessage (ADR-002).

nodes.label: meta.json (four required fields)
nodes.rationale: title / description / difficulty / tags; the platform rejects an upload missing any field, and difficulty must be lowercase.

nodes.label: rebuild() State-Change Pipeline
nodes.rationale: One disciplined path from 'the learner changed something' to 'the scene reflects it'. Ships empty but already runs the disposal/cleanup contract. A single path keeps state flow from drifting and avoids WebGL context exhaustion.

nodes.label: Module-Local ARCHITECTURE / DECISIONS / RULES
nodes.rationale: New files each subject module writes for itself before writing simulation code (not the EG-specific root copies). An undocumented architecture is exactly what lets a module drift from itself as it grows; ADR numbering restarts at ADR-001.

nodes.label: PLATFORM-RULES.md
nodes.rationale: The subject-agnostic enforcement checklist every Simatrix module must follow; a module's own RULES.md is written on top of it as its stated foundation, never duplicating or contradicting it.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md (platform design system)
nodes.rationale: The single platform-wide design system (color tokens, typography, component standards). Modules consume its tokens and must never hard-code design values or carry a local copy.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md (platform product contract)
nodes.rationale: The single platform-wide product contract: personas, design principles, anti-references, and accessibility commitments.

nodes.label: Session Digest Protocol
nodes.rationale: End-of-session digest (what changed, decisions, patterns introduced, open questions, files modified) that feeds the keep-your-own-documents-current discipline.

nodes.label: Scope Boundary (self-contained sim payload)
nodes.rationale: The module produces only the viewport plus its dock/controls/hints; the host website chrome (navbar, browser, account, marketing) is out of scope. Treat the sim as a teaching aid embedded in someone else's page and never render navigation, branding, or footer inside its iframe.

nodes.label: Platform Visual Rules (Quiet Chrome, Chrome-Only Blue, Two-Cue, Two-Weight, Tabular, Flat-Ink, Border-Over-Shadow)
nodes.rationale: The platform's named, subject-agnostic viewport/chrome encodings that still apply to any new discipline; domain-specific meaning is layered on top, never by redefining a shared token.
nodes.norm_label: platform visual rules (quiet chrome, chrome-only blue, two-cue, two-weight, tabular, flat-ink, border-over-shadow)

nodes.label: Dismissible Mobile Notice (<768px)
nodes.rationale: A 'Best experienced on desktop' banner shown below 768px that advises but never blocks the sim; part of the platform runtime contract.

nodes.label: MODULE-STARTER Playbook
nodes.rationale: Start-here playbook for creating a new Simatrix simulation. Exists because Simatrix has no build step, no shared library, and no sync tooling, so hand-made copies will drift unless the right files are copied and only the right ones adapted.

nodes.label: Case A - New Module 2 Topic
nodes.rationale: A new 3D-solids topic in the Engineering Graphics family: copy the whole Module2 master and simplify down, scoping content with the single ENABLED_TIERS flag.

nodes.label: Case B - New Module 1 Topic
nodes.rationale: A new drawing-foundations lesson: not a whole-folder copy but a new thin HTML page + small orchestrator + pure data files served by the one shared engine.js, which is never edited to add a lesson.

nodes.label: Case C - New Subject Module
nodes.rationale: A whole new discipline that does NOT clone Module2/Module1 or share the root ARCHITECTURE/DECISIONS/RULES. It builds a fresh platform skeleton from CLAUDE.module-template.md + PLATFORM-RULES.md and writes its own three docs before development.

nodes.label: Module2 Master (single source of truth)
nodes.rationale: Module2/ is the master and single source of truth; topic folders are its copies (their names don't reveal it). A fix to a shared file belongs in Module2 and must be re-copied, never edited in place, or copies drift (ADR-009).

nodes.label: Module 1 Shared-Engine Pattern
nodes.rationale: One shared engine.js serves seven thin lesson pages; CSS lives in shell.css, not inline. A new lesson supplies data, never an engine edit (ADR-011).

nodes.label: ENABLED_TIERS Scope Flag
nodes.rationale: The single switch in src/problems.js that scopes a topic clone to the tiers it can actually solve (ADR-009); flip it before touching UI so the library and stepper agree on scope.

nodes.label: Byte-Identical Shared Contract Files
nodes.rationale: anim.js, cube/cone/cylinder generators, genericPrism/Pyramid/Solid, meshAnalyzer, vertexLabeler, and the three woff2 fonts are md5-verified identical across the family. Editing a copy in place silently forks the platform; a fix goes in Module2 and is re-copied.

nodes.label: iShape.js Copy-Identical Trap
nodes.rationale: iShape.js looks like a shared contract but Module2's version (larger, imports THREE, carries VP lay-down + inclination) is NOT identical to the topics' smaller version and was never back-copied. Treat it as adapt, not copy-identical (ADR-027).

nodes.label: ZXY Euler Order
nodes.rationale: applyShapeTransform must keep the explicit ZXY Euler order and every ported sign must be re-derived visually (ADR-005), or geometry comes out plausible-but-wrong (mirrored).

nodes.label: Headless Verification (DevTools Protocol)
nodes.rationale: Verify the shipped module by driving Chrome over the DevTools Protocol with Node's built-in WebSocket/fetch, cache disabled, never puppeteer/playwright, verifying the real file (ADR-019). Confirm renderer.info.memory stays flat across 50 rapid regenerations.

nodes.label: index.html <title> to meta.json.title Consistency
nodes.rationale: The <title> must match meta.json.title (browser-tab text + screen-reader name, ADR-026). A shipped Topic 2 inconsistency (title stayed 'Orthographic Projection of Solids' vs meta 'Simple Positions') is the flagged mistake not to repeat.

nodes.label: Orient to Intuition to Problem-solving Arc
nodes.rationale: Every sim must move the learner through Orient -> Intuition -> Problem-solving (PRODUCT.md pedagogy); the first-session build order mirrors this arc.
nodes.norm_label: orient to intuition to problem-solving arc

nodes.label: Design Tokens (Modern Drafting Bench)
nodes.rationale: The single :root source of truth for every colour, space, radius, and motion value. Neutrals authored in OKLCH and stored as resolved sRGB hex (THREE.Color can't parse oklch); no #000/#fff. JS reads them via getComputedStyle and never hard-codes hex.

nodes.label: Three.js CDN Import Map (pinned 0.160.0)
nodes.rationale: Three.js is loaded as CDN ES modules only, pinned to 0.160.0 from jsDelivr for both 'three' and 'three/addons/'. No build step, no bundler, no npm, no @latest, no UMD global (ADR-001); it is the exact contract required by the platform and the sim's only runtime network dependency.

nodes.label: Boot Watchdog + WebGL Fallback
nodes.rationale: A classic script arms a self-healing fallback: if the pinned CDN module is blocked (campus firewall), the connection drops, or WebGL is unavailable, init() never runs and the iframe would sit blank. The learner reads a calm on-brand explanation instead of a void; main.js clears it on a successful boot and a merely-slow load self-heals.

nodes.label: Guided Stepper (step rail + step card)
nodes.rationale: The tutor panel: a vertical numbered step rail (a map you can only walk back along, never skip ahead) beside a step card of progressively disclosed controls. Ships with three placeholder steps to be wired in stepper.js / uiManager.js.

nodes.label: Compare View Scaffolding (card + 50/50 workbench)
nodes.rationale: DOM + CSS scaffolding ported from the Points topic (ADR-012 / ADR-037) making the template natively dual-mode: a floating compact 2D 'drawing sheet' card that expands into a true 50/50 workbench split (body.compare-split grid + #workbench-rail). The enter/exit logic and drawCompare() renderer are NOT ported since this template's main.js is a stub.

nodes.label: Quick-View Camera Buttons (dormant)
nodes.rationale: A segmented pill group (Top/Front/Side) that snaps the ortho camera square to each reference plane; clicking the latched view returns to perspective orbit. Ships HIDDEN in the starter because its projection/fold features were stripped.

nodes.label: Connector-Line Toggle (dormant)
nodes.rationale: A pill toggle that hides the dashed 3D->2D connectors and flattened projectors. Ships HIDDEN alongside the quick-views because the projection feature was stripped from the template.

nodes.label: Textbook Problem Library
nodes.rationale: A full-viewport, focus-trapped dialog whose cards are built by problemLibrary.js from src/problems.js, grouped by tier and filtered to the build's ENABLED_TIERS so a clone only shows solvable problems. The rAF loop pauses while it is open.

nodes.label: Active-Problem Header & Self-Check
nodes.rationale: A quiet paper card (not an accent wash) shown while a textbook problem is loaded: the statement, scaffolded hints revealed one at a time, and a neutral self-check that pops success-green with a check glyph only on a full match. 'Exit problem' clears the framing but never wipes the drawing.

nodes.label: Inline Term Definitions (glossary popover)
nodes.rationale: A dotted-underline word that reveals a plain-language popover on hover/focus/tap so the struggling first-year gets vocabulary defined in place without losing the real term; positioned by terms.js and exposed to screen readers via aria-describedby.

nodes.label: Domain Viewport Colors (HP teal / VP amber / PP violet)
nodes.rationale: Inside-viewport-only projection hues (HP teal solid, VP amber dashed, PP violet) held off the chrome blue, each carrying a non-colour cue (Two-Cue Rule). Consumed by the projection layer; teal<->amber is the CVD-safe pair.
nodes.norm_label: domain viewport colors (hp teal / vp amber / pp violet)

hyperedges.label: Guided Stepper pattern shared across the guided lessons
HP, VP and PP form the orthographic reference-plane framework
BIS line types A / E-F / G / B form the line-type taxonomy
Cinematic Reversible Fold / Rabatment System (First-angle, Points, Lines)
Two-Cue plane colour encoding (teal HP / amber VP / violet PP)
